title: Montezuma County Wells: Depth, Yield and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Montezuma County wells have a 100 ft median depth. See local yields, water levels and modeled finished-well costs of $11,000-$19,500.
h1: What to Expect from a Well in Montezuma County
intro_html:
A well near Cortez may not be a useful cost comparison for a lot outside Mancos or Dolores. Montezuma County has mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground, and reported well depths vary widely. The county median is 100 feet, but the middle half runs from 38 to 200 feet.

Colorado DWR records contain 2,058 permits in the county, with 1,179 recorded as constructed. Use these countywide figures to start a budget, then check nearby completed wells and the permit conditions for the actual parcel.

sections.heading: Depth Around Cortez, Mancos and the Rest of the County
sections.html:
Of the 1,241 wells reporting depth, the median is 100 feet. The middle half spans 38-200 feet, and the 90th-percentile depth is 360 feet. That spread matters more to a drilling bid than the median alone: a contractor needs to allow for the water-bearing material actually encountered, not promise a county-average finish depth.

Mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground can produce different drilling conditions across Montezuma County. Most permit aquifer entries fall into the unnamed/fractured-bedrock category; Dakota and Mancos are also named. Those broad labels do not identify the producing interval beneath your lot. Compare completed wells close to the parcel, particularly those with similar terrain and geology.

sections.heading: A 10 GPM Median Is a Starting Point, Not a Promise
sections.html:
Reported pump yield has a 10.0 gpm median, with the middle half at 5.0-15.0 gpm. Only 226 wells report yield, so this is a smaller sample than the depth records. It describes reported pumping results, not guaranteed year-round production for every permitted well.

At the low end, 4% report under 1 gpm. For a buyer, that is a reason to require a current pumping and recovery test rather than judge the supply by household water pressure. Low production can mean storage and careful demand management. A pressure tank does not establish aquifer capacity, and a reported yield does not authorize irrigation or other uses beyond the permit.

sections.heading: Water Levels Show No Countywide Drop in These Records
sections.html:
The median static water level is 40 feet below ground, with the middle half at 13-80 feet. Static level is where water rests when the well is not pumping; it is not the depth to drill or a measurement of how much water the well can supply.

The median measured level was 40 feet in the 2010s and 40 feet in the 2020s. That series does not show a falling median. However, only 65 wells report static levels, and the decade groups are not necessarily repeated measurements of the same wells. For an existing property near Lewis, Towaoc or elsewhere in the county, look for its own dated measurements and pumping-test results.

sections.heading: Montezuma County's Permit History and Drilling Names
sections.html:
Recorded permit activity reached 366 in the 1990s, followed by 308 in the 2000s and 263 in the 2010s. The records include 142 permits in the 2020s, with the newest permit year listed as 2025. The latest decade is incomplete, so its lower count is not a direct comparison with a full decade.

Mcpherson Drilling Co. (Mcpherson, Billy G.) appears on 217 records, and Ancell Drilling Service (Ancell, Lee) on 93. Another frequent entry, Authorized (Pe, Pg), appears on 149 records but should not be treated as a named drilling business. These are historical record counts, not confirmation of current availability. Domestic/household use accounts for 66% of permits; monitoring accounts for 16%.

sections.heading: Budgeting a New Montezuma County Well
sections.html:
For the county's mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground, the cost model uses $50-$75 per foot. At the 100-foot median depth, that puts the drilled hole at about $5,000-$7,500. A finished well with pump, tank, trenching and electrical is modeled at $11,000-$19,500.

Those are planning figures, not a parcel-specific quote. With the middle half of reported depths spanning 38-200 feet, depth alone can change the scope substantially. Ask the driller to spell out casing, grout, development and testing, along with how additional footage is charged. Have the pump installation, trench route, electrical work and rig access priced clearly so the hole price is not mistaken for a working water system.

sections.heading: Environmental Flags and Site Constraints to Check
sections.html:
The surrounding mapped area includes 24 PFAS sampling/contamination sites, 14 historic mine features and 11 EPA Superfund/cleanup sites within about 10 miles. These are screening flags, not evidence that a particular domestic well is contaminated. A PFAS sampling location is not automatically a confirmed contaminated supply.

Before closing, arrange laboratory testing and review nearby site information to decide whether additional contaminant testing is appropriate. Check the well's casing, sanitary seal and drainage, too. A county median cannot rule out low yield or a dry hole on an undeveloped lot. Plan the septic system, building location, well location and service access together, with required separations verified during local review.

sections.heading: Before Buying a Lot in Dolores, Lewis or Towaoc
sections.html:
Start with the parcel's DWR permit, then match it to the physical well and available construction and pump records. The county has 2,058 permit records but only 1,179 wells recorded as constructed. A permit on the map is not proof of an installed, usable water supply.

Read the permitted uses closely. An exempt household-use permit should not be assumed to cover outdoor watering or livestock; the actual conditions control. For vacant land, confirm permit eligibility with DWR before committing to a building plan. Compare neighboring wells near the property rather than relying on averages from Dolores County or La Plata County. Make water testing, production testing and site feasibility part of your purchase due diligence.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Montezuma County, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported depth is 100 feet, and the middle half of wells runs from 38 to 200 feet. The 90th-percentile depth is 360 feet. These figures come from 1,241 depth reports. For a specific lot, nearby completed wells in similar ground are a better bidding reference than the county median.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Montezuma County?
faq.a: The local model uses $50-$75 per foot for mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground. At the 100-foot median depth, the drilled hole is about $5,000-$7,500, while a finished system with pump, tank, trenching and electrical is about $11,000-$19,500. Actual bids should address depth uncertainty, casing, access and the utility route.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Montezuma County?
faq.a: Among 226 wells reporting pump yield, the median is 10.0 gpm and the middle half is 5.0-15.0 gpm. However, 4% report under 1 gpm. Have an existing well tested for pumping performance and recovery before buying; a historical yield entry does not guarantee current production or establish what uses the permit allows.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Montezuma County?
faq.a: Safety needs to be established for the individual well through laboratory testing. The mapped surrounding area includes 24 PFAS sampling/contamination sites, 14 historic mine features and 11 EPA Superfund/cleanup sites within about 10 miles. Those locations warrant review, but they do not prove contamination in your well. Inspect the wellhead and septic arrangement as well.

faq.q: Is the water table dropping in Montezuma County?
faq.a: The available decade medians do not show a drop: static water levels were 40 feet below ground in both the 2010s and 2020s. Only 65 wells report static levels, though, and these are not necessarily repeat measurements from the same wells. Check the property's own measurement history before drawing conclusions about its water supply.
